docs/data/history/clubs/south-shore.md: South Shore paid players half-a-crown a match
notes: Clubs outside the League lived on friendlies (most Saturdays of the season) and the Cup: friendlies were their main gates, so a friendly draws a larger share of the ground than a League club's, up to its local following (1,500; Everton's 1888 practice game drew 4,000, RECRUITMENT_1888-1900.md 2.2). They paid a part-time groundsman and trainer at most, so a quarter of the base overheads. Every figure is an estimate (D30).
Old boys' clubs: amateurs paying their own way, run on members' subscriptions with small gates; no paid staff, so little of the base overheads. Every figure is an estimate (D30).
